s1.syndrome_frame: Severe metabolic derangement with acute renal failure in a patient with multiple comorbidities
salient_findings: Severe metabolic acidosis with anion gap of 31
Acute renal failure with elevated creatinine
key_facts: Patient has type 2 diabetes mellitus
Patient has hypertension
Patient has ischemic stroke and peripheral arterial disease
Patient has chronic right internal carotid occlusion
Patient has seizures and vascular dementia
Patient was transferred from a nursing home due to decreased oral intake and dehydration
Patient received 1 L of intravenous normal saline en route
Patient's blood pressure was 94/49 mmHg initially and 101/59 mmHg on arrival
Patient's heart rate was 105 beats per minute
Patient's respiratory rate was 17 breaths per minute
Patient's oxygen saturation was 100% on room air
Patient has dry mucous membranes and appears sarcopenic
Patient's sodium level was 145 mEq/L
Patient's potassium level was 6.6 mEq/L
Patient's blood urea nitrogen was 207 mg/dL
Patient's creatinine was 10.2 mg/dL with a baseline of 1.1 mg/dL
Patient's glucose level was 185 mg/dL
Patient's lactate level was 4.4 mmol/L
Patient's venous pH was 7.09
Patient's home medications include insulin glargine, insulin aspart, and empagliflozin

shortlist.label: Diabetic ketoacidosis
shortlist.why_kept: Patient has type 2 diabetes mellitus and elevated β-hydroxybutyrate level

shortlist.label: Lactic acidosis
shortlist.why_kept: Patient has severe metabolic acidosis and elevated lactate level

shortlist.label: Uremic acidosis
shortlist.why_kept: Patient has acute renal failure and elevated creatinine level

shortlist.label: Prerenal acute kidney injury
shortlist.why_kept: Patient has severe dehydration and hypovolemia

shortlist.label: Starvation ketosis
shortlist.why_kept: Patient has decreased oral intake and dehydration for at least one week

raw.rationale: The patient's severe metabolic acidosis with an anion gap of 31, elevated creatinine of 10.2 mg/dL, and hyperkalemia are more consistent with uremic acidosis, especially given the context of acute renal failure and dehydration.

rejected.label: Diabetic ketoacidosis
rejected.why: While the patient has type 2 diabetes and an elevated β-hydroxybutyrate level, the presence of severe acute renal failure and the lack of significant hyperglycemia (glucose 185 mg/dL) make diabetic ketoacidosis less likely as the primary cause of the metabolic acidosis.

rejected.label: Lactic acidosis
rejected.why: Although the patient has an elevated lactate level, the clinical context and the severity of the metabolic acidosis are more suggestive of uremic acidosis than lactic acidosis alone.

rejected.label: Prerenal acute kidney injury
rejected.why: The patient's acute renal failure is more consistent with intrinsic renal damage given the significant elevation in creatinine and the presence of uremic acidosis, rather than a prerenal cause alone.

rejected.label: Starvation ketosis
rejected.why: While the patient has been experiencing decreased oral intake, the severity of the metabolic acidosis and the presence of uremia suggest that starvation ketosis is not the primary cause of the acidosis.
